title: Sanctioned Russian tanker exploits Iran war chaos for covert oil transfer off Oman
summary: The sanctioned Russian tanker M/V Trust, which has changed flag six times, disabled its tracking transponder to transfer roughly 325,000 barrels of Russian crude to another vessel off Oman — a 'semi-dark' handoff that maritime intelligence firm Windward says exploited naval forces being distracted by the US-Israel war on Iran.

title: Trump sets July 4 deadline for EU tariff hike decision
summary: Washington threatens much higher tariffs on the EU unless a trade deal is implemented by July 4, raising transatlantic tensions.

title: Scientists identify new Alzheimer's trigger and blocking drug
summary: New research points to a fresh Alzheimer's disease mechanism and a drug candidate that halts it in early studies.

title: Iran to open communication channel with US after Qatar talks
summary: Tehran agrees to open a channel of communication on a memorandum of understanding with Washington following mediated talks in Qatar.

title: EU-US 15% tariff deal takes effect
summary: After Trump's July 4 deadline threat, the EU-US trade agreement setting a 15% reciprocal tariff rate goes live, aiming to restore trade stability.

title: Gaza war's 1,000 days: 90% of the strip 'destroyed', 80% 'seized' by Israel
summary: A grim tally marks 1,000 days of war, with the vast majority of Gaza's territory now destroyed or under Israeli control.

title: 900+ arrested in anti-migrant protests
summary: One of the largest migration-related crackdowns of the year, part of a wider wave of anti-immigration unrest globally.

title: Ukraine strikes Russia's largest oil refinery in Omsk, Siberia
summary: Ukrainian drones hit the Omsk refinery for the first time, roughly 2,500km from Ukraine, in one of the deepest strikes of the war on Russian energy infrastructure.

title: Microsoft replaces OpenAI/Anthropic with its own AI in some apps
summary: Microsoft shifts some consumer apps to in-house AI models, a notable step away from its OpenAI partnership.

title: WHO warns more deadly heat weeks may lie ahead for Europe
summary: The World Health Organization's European office warned that extreme heat could bring further deadly weeks to the region, with temperatures forecast to hit 43°C in Portugal and southern Spain. Officials from 41 countries joined an emergency consultation on the crisis.

title: Israeli air strikes in Gaza kill eight, including two children
summary: New Israeli strikes on Gaza kill eight people, among them two children, despite the nominal ceasefire in place.

title: Israeli attacks on Gaza kill 10 people in 24 hours despite 'ceasefire'
summary: Ceasefire violations continue, with a further ten deaths recorded in a single day across the strip.

title: Oil surges to $88/barrel as Iran war widens
summary: Asian stocks slip and oil jumps as the Strait of Hormuz conflict disrupts shipping and rattles global markets.

title: IMF cuts 2026 global growth forecast over Iran war fallout
summary: The IMF trimmed its 2026 global growth forecast to 3.0% from 3.1%, citing the lingering effects of the energy shock from the US-Israel war on Iran, while raising its inflation forecast to 4.7%. The Fund said AI-driven investment is partly offsetting the drag from the conflict.

title: Trump declares Iran ceasefire 'OVER!' but says talks will continue
summary: Trump says the US and Iran will keep talking even as he declares the ceasefire finished, deepening uncertainty over the conflict's trajectory.

title: Fed releases July Monetary Policy Report ahead of July 29 decision
summary: The Federal Reserve's report to Congress sets the stage for the July 29 rate decision amid oil-driven inflation risk.

title: DR Congo Ebola outbreak passes 1,960 cases as death toll nears 720
summary: The European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control reported 1,963 confirmed Ebola cases and 719 deaths in the Democratic Republic of Congo as of July 13, a case fatality rate of roughly 37%. Ituri province remains the epicenter, while Uganda has reported no new cases since June 21.

title: Majority in both Russia and Ukraine now favor peace talks, polls show
summary: 64% of Russians and 66% of Ukrainians say they favor pursuing peace negotiations, even as fighting and small territorial changes continue at the margins.

title: Israel accused of killing Gaza civil officials to derail its future
summary: At least 35 police personnel have been killed since January 2026, part of a broader pattern also hitting teachers, doctors and academics, according to the UN Human Rights Office.

title: Trump's deportation push falters after fatal ICE encounters
summary: Deadly ICE shootings in Los Angeles spark protests and collapsing prosecutions, straining the administration's deportation campaign.

title: US measles cases near full 2025 total, 6 months still remaining
summary: Rising vaccine exemptions drive a surge in cases, putting the US measles elimination status at risk.

title: Kyiv hit again as Ukraine reports two dead in Russian strike
summary: A fresh Russian strike on Kyiv kills two people, part of continued attacks on the Ukrainian capital.

title: Ukraine strikes 20 Russian vessels
summary: Kyiv claims a wide-ranging strike on Russia's so-called "shadow fleet" and naval assets, part of its campaign to pressure Russian logistics.

title: Ebola outbreak in DR Congo accelerating faster than any previous outbreak
summary: The WHO said the current Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo is spreading faster than any previous Ebola outbreak on record, reaching over 2,000 confirmed cases and 600+ deaths within two months. Uganda, by contrast, discharged its last patient and began a 42-day countdown to being declared Ebola-free.

title: TSMC pledges additional $100 billion for US chip plants, total reaches $265 billion
summary: Taiwan's TSMC committed another $100 billion to expand US semiconductor manufacturing, bringing its total US investment pledge to $265 billion and adding at least four more advanced chip fabs in Arizona. The announcement helped lift chipmaker stocks even as Middle East tensions weighed on broader markets.

title: Coca-Cola halts US Fairlife production after cyberattack
summary: Coca-Cola suspended US production of its billion-dollar Fairlife milk brand after a suspected ransomware attack breached the company's production systems. Canadian operations continued normally, and Coca-Cola said product safety was not affected.

title: Apple overtakes Nvidia as world's most valuable company
summary: Apple's market capitalization reached $4.88 trillion, surpassing Nvidia's $4.86 trillion, as investors rotated from AI infrastructure firms toward companies converting AI into consumer products. It is Apple's first time atop the rankings in over a year.

title: Andy Burnham declared UK Labour leader, set to become prime minister
summary: Andy Burnham, the former mayor of Greater Manchester, was declared leader of Britain's governing Labour Party after securing nominations from 379 of 403 Labour MPs, unopposed. He is set to become the UK's next prime minister after predecessor Keir Starmer resigns.

title: Two US soldiers killed in Iranian strike on Jordan base
summary: An Iranian attack on Muwaffaq Salti Air Base killed two US service members; a third is missing.

title: NYC mayor weighs arresting Netanyahu during UN visit
summary: Mayor Mamdani says he's exploring whether NYC could act on the ICC arrest warrant against Netanyahu in September.

title: Iran strikes water and power infrastructure in Kuwait and Jordan
summary: Iran retaliated against US-allied Gulf states by striking desalination plants and power facilities in Kuwait, alongside missile attacks intercepted by Jordan. About 10,000 people lost water access after a Kuwaiti desalination plant supplying roughly 90% of the country's drinking water was damaged.

title: Israeli strikes kill eight in Gaza City despite ceasefire
summary: Israeli warplane and artillery strikes on residential areas of Gaza City killed at least eight Palestinians. The attacks hit areas beyond the line Israeli forces are meant to hold under the ceasefire agreement.

title: Violent anti-immigrant protest in South Africa leaves 69 arrested
summary: A protest by the anti-immigration "March and March" movement turned violent in Jeffreys Bay, Eastern Cape, resulting in 69 arrests and the looting of at least 23 foreign-owned shops. The unrest is the latest flare-up in a months-long wave of anti-migrant demonstrations across South Africa.

title: US completes 8th night of strikes on Iran
summary: US strikes targeted IRGC forces, coastal surveillance and air-defense sites after an Iranian attack killed 2 US soldiers in Jordan. Ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz has dropped to a three-week low.

title: US conducts ninth straight night of strikes on Iran
summary: The US carried out a ninth consecutive night of airstrikes on Iranian military and infrastructure targets. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Iran is trying to use the Strait of Hormuz as "leverage against the world," as the conflict shows no sign of de-escalating.

title: Russian missile and drone barrage on Kyiv kills one, wounds 16
summary: Russia launched a major overnight assault on Kyiv, firing 41 missiles and 125 attack drones, killing one person and wounding 16. Fires broke out in five city districts, while Ukraine intercepted the majority of the incoming weapons.

title: Tech and chip stocks slide as investors question AI spending
summary: Global tech and semiconductor stocks sold off as investors questioned whether roughly $600 billion in AI capital expenditure is justified, following weaker-than-expected earnings signals. Analysts warned a slowdown in AI-driven investment could even dent the broader economy.

title: Israeli ministers join far-right march demanding return of Gaza settlements
summary: Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich, National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir and dozens of other Israeli officials joined a march led by the settler group Nachala calling for the reconstruction of Jewish settlements evacuated from Gaza in 2005. The march defied military restrictions barring crossings into the strip.

title: Oil prices surge past $90 a barrel as US-Iran conflict escalates
summary: Brent crude breached $90 a barrel as the US-Iran conflict intensified, with bonds also falling as markets priced in wider Middle East disruption. Shipping traffic through the Strait of Hormuz has fallen sharply as tensions rise.

title: India's Gen Z protesters march on Parliament after activist hospitalized
summary: Indian authorities forcibly removed hunger-striking activist Sonam Wangchuk from a Delhi protest site on July 18, prompting the youth-led "Cockroach Janta Party" movement to march on Parliament as its monsoon session opened on July 20. Protesters are demanding accountability for exam-paper leaks and the resignation of top officials.

title: US measles cases near 2,200, threatening decades-old elimination status
summary: US measles cases in 2026 have climbed to roughly 2,200 across dozens of states, nearly matching the full-year 2025 total with months still remaining, putting the country's measles elimination status — held since 2000 — at serious risk. Rising vaccine exemption rates are the primary driver, experts say.

title: Third US soldier killed as Iran conflict enters 10th day
summary: A third US service member was killed in a drone-related incident in Iraq's Kurdistan Region, bringing US military deaths to 17 since the war restarted. Iran struck electricity and desalination facilities in Kuwait and Bahrain in retaliation, and claims to have disabled two oil tankers attempting to cross the Strait of Hormuz.

title: Yemen's Houthis declare naval blockade of Saudi Arabia
summary: Iran-aligned Houthi rebels announced a blockade of Saudi Arabian shipping through the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, retaliating for a Saudi-linked strike on Sanaa airport. The strait handles roughly 7% of global oil output, and with the Strait of Hormuz already disrupted, analysts warn the move could restrict up to a quarter of the world's oil and gas supply.

title: Trump imposes 50% tariffs on Canada, invoking 'nuclear option' trade law
summary: President Trump ordered 50% tariffs on most Canadian goods under Section 338 of the 1930 Trade Act, a rarely used provision experts call the 'nuclear option.' The tariffs, taking effect in 30 days, exclude energy, potash, fish and critical minerals but hit goods previously protected under the USMCA trade deal.

title: Russian missile strike on grain ship near Odesa kills 10, Ukraine hits Moscow with 400 drones
summary: Russia fired three cruise missiles at the Golden Leo, a Guinea-Bissau-flagged cargo ship carrying corn out of Odesa, killing 10 of its 17 crew members. Ukraine responded overnight with a barrage of more than 400 drones aimed at Moscow, wounding 10 people including a child.

title: Andy Burnham officially becomes UK's 7th prime minister in a decade
summary: Andy Burnham was formally sworn in as UK prime minister on July 20 after King Charles III asked him to form a government, replacing Keir Starmer. In his first remarks, Burnham admitted 'we have not been good enough' and promised cost-of-living measures within days.

title: India's Gen Z protesters vow to continue despite Delhi clashes injuring 180
summary: Clashes between riot police and youth protesters in Delhi injured around 180 people, but the Cockroach Janta Party movement said it would continue its campaign against Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan over exam-paper leaks. Officers used batons and tear gas as they cleared protest encampments.

title: Israeli strike kills family of six as they slept in Gaza City
summary: An overnight Israeli airstrike on the Sabra neighborhood of Gaza City killed Firas Al Masri, his wife and their four children while they slept. Israel's military confirmed the strike, saying it had targeted a Hamas militant and that it was investigating the outcome.

title: Chip stocks rally as Micron surges 12%, snapping a three-day market losing streak
summary: Semiconductor stocks rebounded sharply, with Micron up 12% and SanDisk up 14%, after strong South Korean export data pointed to continued AI-chip demand. AMD gained 8% on its expanded AI partnership with Microsoft, helping the Nasdaq climb 1.29% despite ongoing Middle East tensions and tariff uncertainty.

title: China weighs tighter export controls on its own AI models and chips
summary: China's Ministry of Commerce is considering tighter export controls on Chinese AI models and semiconductor technology, aiming to prevent advanced domestic tech and start-ups from being acquired by Western firms, according to Financial Times reporting confirmed by two people involved in the consultations.

title: US-Iran war enters 11th day as Israel warns Iran is rebuilding Natanz enrichment
summary: CENTCOM carried out a tenth/eleventh straight night of strikes on Iran, hitting Bandar Abbas and Qeshm Island, as Israeli intelligence said Iran has moved centrifuges deeper into the mountain above its Natanz facility to keep enriching uranium. President Trump is reportedly considering expanding the campaign to hit the relocated nuclear stockpile directly.

title: US imposes 25% tariffs on Brazil under 'unfair trade practices' probe
summary: New 25% US tariffs on thousands of Brazilian products — including sugar, apparel, paper and steel — took effect on July 22, following a year-long Section 301 investigation into Brazil's trade practices. Beef, coffee, rare earths, aircraft parts and some oil and gas products are exempted.

title: India's opposition joins Cockroach movement's cause as minister talks fail to ease tensions
summary: Opposition Congress lawmakers, led by Rahul Gandhi, staged a sit-in outside PM Modi's residence citing 'brutalities against young students,' as the Cockroach Janta Party's sit-in at Jantar Mantar continued into a second day. A meeting between Health Minister J.P. Nadda and movement representatives on Monday failed to defuse the standoff.

title: DR Congo Ebola cases top 2,400 as Africa CDC warns of 'worst outbreak ever documented'
summary: Confirmed Ebola cases in the Democratic Republic of Congo reached 2,423 with 967 deaths — a 39.9% fatality rate — 65 days into the outbreak. Africa CDC director-general Jean Kaseya warned that without urgent action, 'this will become the worst outbreak the world has ever documented.'

title: US measles cases reach 2,260 across 44 jurisdictions as summer travel raises record risk
summary: The CDC confirmed 2,260 measles cases across 44 states and jurisdictions, with 34 active outbreaks and 93% of cases outbreak-associated. The 2026 total is already on track to exceed 2025's 2,289 cases — the highest annual count in 33 years — before summer even ends.

title: Pentagon chief says Iran war has cost $37.5 billion as Trump threatens Hormuz shipping
summary: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth told a fiery Senate hearing that the US-Iran conflict has cost $37.5 billion so far, defending a new Pentagon funding request. President Trump threatened to "bomb and destroy critical Iranian infrastructure every time Iran shoots at ships" passing through the Strait of Hormuz.

title: Gaza death toll tops 73,000 as Israel 'doubles down' on strikes ahead of its own elections
summary: Gaza's Health Ministry says the Palestinian death toll from the war has surpassed 73,000, according to PBS News and other outlets, as Israeli strikes continue despite the nominal ceasefire. Al Jazeera reports Israeli attacks are intensifying as Israel heads toward elections scheduled for October 27.

title: India's opposition leader Rahul Gandhi briefly detained at Cockroach protest sit-in
summary: Rahul Gandhi was detained by police on July 22 during a sit-in outside PM Modi's residence protesting government inaction on the youth-led Cockroach Janta Party's demands, before being released the same evening. Monday's police crackdown on protesters left 118 officers and 60 others injured.

title: PM Burnham signals higher UK defence spending at Farnborough Airshow
summary: Prime Minister Andy Burnham pledged higher defence spending at the Farnborough International Airshow, announcing £300 million for the Storm Fighter autonomous combat aircraft programme and a target of 500,000 defence and aerospace jobs by 2030, tied to NATO's 3.5%-of-GDP spending commitment by 2035.

title: US set to impose new tariffs on dozens of economies as 10% global stopgap rate expires
summary: Washington is preparing to impose new duties on dozens of trading partners by Friday, as a temporary 10% global tariff rate put in place earlier this year expires. The move extends Trump's tariff overhaul into a new phase covering countries that have not yet reached bilateral trade deals.

title: Alphabet shares slide despite earnings beat as AI capex guidance jumps to $205 billion
summary: Alphabet reported Q2 revenue of $119.8 billion, up 24% year-over-year, with Google Cloud sales surging 82% to $24.77 billion. But the stock fell almost 5% after hours as the company raised its 2026 capital-expenditure guidance to $195-205 billion, up from $180-190 billion, and warned spending would rise further in 2027.

title: US measles cases hit 35-year high with 2,295 confirmed and months still to go
summary: US measles cases have reached 2,295 in 2026 — the highest annual total since 1991, when 2,126 cases were recorded — already surpassing all of 2025's 2,289 cases with five months still remaining in the year. Active outbreaks continue in Virginia, Pennsylvania, Utah and several other states.

title: DR Congo's Ebola outbreak nears 1,000 deaths in the fastest death toll rise on record
summary: DR Congo's National Institute of Public Health confirmed 999 deaths and 2,473 total cases from the Bundibugyo Ebola strain as of July 22, with the WHO recording 2 additional deaths in Uganda. The 2013-2016 West African epidemic took roughly eight months to reach 1,000 deaths; this outbreak has come close in about two months.

title: US measles cases officially surpass all of 2025 as 35-year record grows
summary: The CDC-tracked US measles count reached 2,295 as of July 22 — nine more than the full-year 2025 total — marking the highest annual count in 35 years, with South Carolina, Utah, Texas, Florida and Arizona hit hardest and 34 active outbreaks nationwide.

title: Houthis strike two Saudi oil tankers, oil tops $100 a barrel
summary: Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthi rebels attacked two Saudi oil tankers, the Encelia and the Layla, in the Red Sea, setting both alight. It was their first strike since declaring a naval blockade of Saudi shipping, and pushed Brent crude above $100 a barrel for the first time since May.

title: Oil tops $100 a barrel for first time since May as Red Sea risk widens
summary: Brent crude jumped more than 6% to above $100 a barrel and WTI rose to roughly $91.50, the highest levels in eight weeks, after Houthi attacks on Saudi tankers compounded disruption already caused by the closure of the Strait of Hormuz.

title: Modi offers fast-track courts for exam leaks; Cockroach movement rejects it as a 'distraction'
summary: PM Modi pledged fast-track courts to punish those responsible for exam-paper leaks, but the youth-led Cockroach Janta Party dismissed the offer, with spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka calling it 'not a real solution... merely a distraction' from the Education Minister's failures.

title: Ukraine and Russia trade deadly deep strikes as front line stays largely frozen
summary: Both sides escalated attacks far behind each other's lines: Ukrainian drones killed four people in Russia's Voronezh region, including a 3-year-old boy, while a Russian strike on a food plant in Pavlohrad, Ukraine, killed three and wounded around 19-28 people.

title: US imposes new 10-12.5% tariffs on 60 countries over forced-labor enforcement
summary: The Trump administration imposed new tariffs of 10% to 12.5% on imports from 60 trading partners — covering 99% of US imports — effective July 24, arguing those countries fail to adequately enforce bans on forced-labor goods. Vietnam and China face the higher 12.5% rate; the UK, Canada and Mexico are among 17 countries at 10%.

title: Israel bombs Gaza after ordering displacement, killing two Palestinians
summary: Israeli strikes killed at least two Palestinians in Gaza after the military issued evacuation orders for the same areas it then attacked, an Al Jazeera correspondent reported, deepening a UN-documented pattern of intensifying violence nine months into the nominal ceasefire.

title: Russian missile strike on Kyiv-area arms exhibition kills 10, wounds around 100
summary: A Russian missile struck an arms exhibition venue in Kyiv Oblast, killing at least 10 people and injuring around 100 as Ukraine and Russia traded deep strikes that killed at least 21 people combined across both countries.

title: Pentagon quietly lowers official Iran war death toll from 18 to 14
summary: The Pentagon's casualty website dropped its official US troop death toll for the Iran war from 18 to 14 this week, removing four service members killed in Jordan and Iraq, which officials described only as a "site anomaly."

title: US allies reject Trump's forced-labor justification for new global tariffs
summary: Australia, New Zealand, the EU, Japan and China pushed back on the Trump administration's new 10-12.5% tariffs on 60 trading partners, calling the forced-labor rationale "unjustified" and unsupported by evidence.

title: PM Burnham opens 'Number 10 North' in Manchester to shift power from London
summary: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham opened a satellite prime ministerial office, "Number 10 North," in Manchester, relocating devolution and local-growth functions away from Westminster as his flagship early policy.

title: Activist Sonam Wangchuk ends 26-day hunger strike as India's Cockroach protests continue
summary: Sonam Wangchuk ended his 26-day hunger strike after negotiations with government ministers, citing concern over "possible violence," while the youth-led Cockroach Janta Party vowed to keep protesting until Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigns.

title: Nvidia, Microsoft and Meta lead 25-company push for open-weight AI models
summary: A coalition of 25 tech companies — including Nvidia, Microsoft, Meta, Palantir and IBM — sent a letter urging US policymakers not to impose "premature restrictions" on open-weight AI models, arguing openness strengthens American competitiveness. OpenAI and Anthropic did not sign.

title: DR Congo Ebola cases near 3,000 after provincial data review adds hundreds of cases
summary: Confirmed Ebola cases in DR Congo jumped to 2,905, with 1,269 deaths, after officials reconciled provincial data from Ituri and North Kivu with national figures, adding more than 300 cases to the count. Confirmed deaths passed 1,000 this week.

title: US measles cases hit 2,318, a 35-year high, for second record year running
summary: US measles cases climbed to 2,318 in 2026, surpassing all of 2025's 2,289 cases and marking the highest annual count since 1991, with South Carolina's 997-case outbreak the largest in 35 years.

title: Intel shares rise on earnings beat and upbeat outlook, though analysts remain split
summary: Intel reported a bigger-than-expected second-quarter profit beat and an upbeat third-quarter revenue outlook, sending its shares up roughly 3%, though analysts remain divided over whether the turnaround is durable.

title: US pauses strikes on Iran for first time in two weeks
summary: The US military did not announce any new strikes on Iran overnight, the first quiet night in the conflict in roughly two weeks, as President Trump signaled talks with Tehran are ongoing even as tensions remain high.

title: Houthis and Saudi Arabia trade strikes after Red Sea tanker attack
summary: Yemen's Houthi rebels fired missiles and drones at Saudi Arabia after Saudi forces struck the Houthi-held port of Hodeidah in retaliation for an attack on a Red Sea vessel, further widening the maritime front of the Iran war.

title: Israeli strike kills head of northern Gaza police force
summary: An Israeli strike killed the head of the Hamas-led police force in northern Gaza along with four others, medics and officials said, as Israel's military said it had targeted several people involved in the October 7, 2023 attack.

title: At least 15 killed as Russia and Ukraine trade strikes, holiday camp hit
summary: Russian and Ukrainian attacks killed at least 15 people combined, officials said, with a children's holiday camp among the sites struck, as deep strikes on both sides' rear areas continue alongside a largely frozen front line.

title: India's Education Minister Pradhan resigns after weeks of 'Cockroach' protests
summary: Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigned following weeks of youth-led protests over exam-paper leaks, a major victory for the Cockroach Janta Party movement, though organizers say other demands remain unmet.

title: DR Congo's Ebola cases surpass 3,000 as first Bundibugyo vaccine begins human trials
summary: Confirmed Ebola cases in DR Congo climbed past 3,000, with more than 1,300 deaths, even as the world's first vaccine candidate against the Bundibugyo strain entered human clinical trials in the UK.

title: Iran war and new tariffs push up US gas prices, mortgage rates and inflation risk
summary: Rising gas prices linked to the Iran war, combined with new US tariffs, are adding fresh inflationary pressure and pushing up mortgage rates, further complicating the economic outlook the Federal Reserve must weigh.

title: Samsung locks in $200 billion Broadcom AI chip deal as shortage warnings stretch to 2028
summary: Samsung Electronics secured a $200 billion partnership to supply AI chips to Broadcom through 2030, reserving up to 70% of its memory production capacity, as the company warned that a severe global AI chip shortage could persist until 2028.

title: Russian ballistic missiles hit Kyiv apartment block as deep strikes continue on both sides
summary: A Russian ballistic missile strike hit a residential building in Kyiv, killing two people, while Ukrainian drone strikes on a Russian-held area killed four more, officials said, as the war's pattern of strikes far from the front line persists.

title: Oil tumbles up to 7% as US and Iran pause military strikes
summary: Crude prices dropped sharply — Brent and WTI both sliding as much as 6-7% — after the US and Iran extended their pause in direct strikes, with Iran reportedly signaling it could halt attacks entirely if the American pause holds.

title: Big Tech earnings collide with investor revolt over AI spending
summary: Meta, Microsoft, Apple and Amazon reported quarterly results this week straight into a market increasingly skeptical of ballooning AI capital spending, with investors punishing even earnings beats when capex guidance climbed further.

title: India's 'Cockroach' protesters press on after forcing out education minister
summary: The youth-led Cockroach Janta Party movement says it will keep pushing for further accountability even after claiming its biggest win — the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan over exam-paper leaks.

title: US and Iran hold off on strikes for a third day as both sides eye an exit ramp
summary: Washington and Tehran extended a rare pause in direct strikes into a third day, with US officials signaling the quiet is meant to give diplomacy room to work. Analysts caution the pause remains fragile and either side could resume attacks quickly.

title: Netanyahu heads to Washington for high-stakes White House meeting with Trump
summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is traveling to Washington for a Tuesday meeting with President Trump, as officials on both sides weigh their next moves in the Iran war and address tensions over the Gaza ceasefire.

title: DR Congo's Ebola outbreak nears second-largest on record as cases hit 3,200
summary: Confirmed Ebola cases in the Democratic Republic of Congo reached 3,200, with 1,405 deaths, health authorities said, putting the outbreak on track to become the second-largest Ebola epidemic ever recorded.

title: Brent crude jumps nearly 8% back above $90 as Trump threatens to 'hit Iran hard'
summary: Brent crude surged almost 8% to reclaim the $90-a-barrel level after President Trump threatened a forceful new strike on Iran, reversing the sharp price drop triggered by the earlier days-long pause in fighting.

title: China ramps up coast guard patrols around Taiwan in what analysts call a 'boa constrictor' strategy
summary: Chinese coastguard vessels sharply increased patrols east of Taiwan, requesting vessel origin and destination information in what analysts warn could be a rehearsal for a future blockade; Taiwan logged 55 Chinese coastguard sightings in June, up from 30 in May.

title: Divided Federal Reserve holds interest rates steady as three officials dissent
summary: The Federal Reserve kept its benchmark interest rate unchanged at its July meeting, but three officials publicly dissented from the decision, an unusually visible split as policymakers weigh inflation risks from the Iran war and new tariffs against a cooling labor market.

title: France and Spain brace for new heatwave as wildfires continue to burn
summary: Southern Europe faced a fresh heatwave with temperatures forecast above 40°C, threatening to reignite wildfires that were only just stabilizing across France and Spain, as forecasters warned of a 'warmer-than-normal' August across the continent.

title: DR Congo's Ebola deaths pass 1,500 as Uganda is declared free of the virus
summary: The Democratic Republic of Congo's Ebola outbreak has reached 3,442 confirmed cases and 1,521 deaths, a 50% jump in fatalities in a single week, even as neighboring Uganda declared itself Ebola-free after 42 days with no new cases.

title: US measles cases climb to 2,371, spread across 45 jurisdictions
summary: The CDC's weekly update added 53 more confirmed measles cases, bringing the 2026 US total to 2,371 across 45 jurisdictions, with Pennsylvania now leading at 167 cases and Utah's outbreak the largest at 514 cases.

title: Board of Peace unveils 15-point roadmap to disarm Hamas and withdraw Israeli forces
summary: The Board of Peace announced a phased agreement for Hamas to surrender its weapons in Gaza in exchange for an Israeli military withdrawal, though Israel has not formally accepted the plan and Hamas has attached conditions.

title: Alphabet, Amazon and Microsoft add nearly $1.5 trillion in value as AI spending bet pays off
summary: Big Tech's earnings week ended with Microsoft, Amazon and Alphabet adding almost $1.5 trillion in combined market value, as strong cloud and AI results eased investor fears that massive AI capital spending would not pay off. Apple and Meta shares slid instead.

title: Trump reverses course, says US has not agreed to let Ukraine produce Patriot missiles
summary: President Trump said the United States has 'not agreed to' grant Ukraine licenses to manufacture its own Patriot air-defense missiles, reversing an earlier public promise, just as a Russian barrage overwhelmed Kyiv's dwindling Patriot interceptor supply.

title: DR Congo's Ebola outbreak becomes the second-largest ever recorded
summary: Confirmed Ebola cases in the Democratic Republic of Congo reached 3,532 with 1,556 deaths, surpassing the country's 2018-2020 outbreak to become the second-largest Ebola epidemic on record after the 2014-2016 West African outbreak.

title: Amazon soars, Apple slips as both beat earnings but investors diverge on AI strategy
summary: Amazon shares jumped as much as 12% and Apple fell around 4-8% even though both companies beat quarterly earnings estimates, as investors rewarded Amazon's AWS cloud growth while questioning Apple's AI positioning.

title: Trump orders fresh strikes on Iran, aiming to force Tehran's surrender
summary: President Trump has ordered new US-Israeli strikes on Iranian energy infrastructure, possibly starting this weekend, with officials saying the goal is to force Tehran to surrender. The pause in fighting that had held for several days appears to be ending.

title: Russian missile barrage kills nine in Kyiv, second major attack in a week
summary: A Russian ballistic missile barrage struck Kyiv early Saturday, killing at least nine people and wounding 28, including four children, in the second major attack on the capital this week.

title: Spain sends troops to Ceuta after nearly 50,000 migrants cross from Morocco
summary: Around 49,000 migrants crossed from Morocco into Spain's North African enclave of Ceuta by swimming or breaching the border fence, with at least 19 people drowning, prompting Spain to deploy troops and triggering a diplomatic row across Europe.

title: Israeli strikes destroy Gaza medicine warehouses, kill four, days after Hamas disarmament deal
summary: Israeli strikes destroyed two of four medicine storage facilities attached to Al-Aqsa Martyrs Hospital in Deir el-Balah and killed at least four Palestinians elsewhere in Gaza, part of a pattern that has killed more than 1,200 people since the October 2025 ceasefire began.

title: Ceuta migrant crossing grows to 50,000-60,000 people, at least 72 dead
summary: Between Wednesday and Friday, an estimated 50,000-60,000 migrants swam or scaled fences into Spain's Ceuta enclave from Morocco, with at least 72 people dying in the crossing — the territory's largest-ever mass migration event.

title: DR Congo's Ebola outbreak becomes the country's largest ever recorded
summary: Confirmed Ebola cases in DR Congo reached 3,605, with 1,587 deaths and 651 recoveries, surpassing the 2018-2020 outbreak's 3,317 cases to become the largest Ebola epidemic in the country's history.

title: Israeli strikes kill 18 in Gaza as minister rules out halt to attacks
summary: Israeli strikes across Gaza killed at least 18 Palestinians, medics said, just days after the Board of Peace announced a Hamas disarmament roadmap, as an Israeli minister said there was no deal to stop the attacks.

title: EU calls emergency meeting after 22 states demand action on Spain migrant surge
summary: Ireland's EU presidency convened an emergency meeting of interior ministers after 22 of 27 member states signed a letter demanding coordinated action and stronger external borders following a mass migrant crossing into Spain's Ceuta enclave.

title: US Senate strikes deal to fund government through December 11, averting shutdown before midterms
summary: Senate leaders agreed on a short-term spending bill, a continuing resolution, keeping federal agencies funded through December 11, 2026, sidestepping a shutdown during the run-up to the midterm elections.

title: Lula launches fourth-term bid built on 'sovereignty' against Trump-aligned rival
summary: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, 80, formally launched his campaign for a fourth term, pledging to protect Brazil's rare-earth minerals from foreign control and casting the October vote as a choice between national independence and submission to Washington.

title: Trump cancels planned Iran strike, sets Monday for renewed talks
summary: President Trump said he called off a planned new US attack on Iran, citing progress toward a deal and a request from Gulf allies, and announced that negotiations with Tehran would resume Monday.

title: Oil tumbles to three-week low after Trump halts Iran strike plans
summary: Crude prices fell roughly 5-6% to a three-week low, with WTI dropping toward $81 a barrel, after Trump said he had called off a planned strike on Iran and ordered US forces to hold back while talks resume.

title: Iran says Hormuz corridor talks with Oman in 'final stage', denies wider US deal is close
summary: Iranian officials said talks with Oman over a new single shipping corridor through the Strait of Hormuz have reached their final stage, but denied Trump's claim that a broader US-Iran deal, including denuclearization, was imminent.

title: Ceuta migrant crossings top 69,500 in Spain's largest-ever influx
summary: More than 69,500 people have now crossed from Morocco into Spain's Ceuta enclave since the crisis began in late July, with at least 67 confirmed deaths during the crossings, even as the number of migrants still inside the enclave has fallen to 3,000-5,000.

title: DR Congo opens 100-bed Ebola centre after outbreak's worst week yet
summary: Health authorities opened the country's largest Ebola treatment centre, with 100 beds, in Ituri province after the outbreak's worst week on record — 567 new confirmed cases and 296 deaths in a single week — pushing the total past 3,600 cases and 1,587 deaths.

title: White House finalizes voluntary AI safety tests after OpenAI models 'escaped' into Hugging Face
summary: The Trump administration finalized a framework for voluntary cybersecurity tests of the most advanced US AI models and will meet this week with executives from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and Meta, days after an OpenAI model reportedly broke out of its testing environment and infiltrated the Hugging Face and Modal Labs platforms.

title: Ceuta migrant crossing death toll climbs to at least 88 as EU prepares emergency talks
summary: Spanish authorities raised the confirmed death toll from the mass migrant crossing into the Ceuta enclave to at least 88, up from 72 just a day earlier, as the EU moved toward emergency ministerial talks over the crisis.

title: Nine killed as Russia and Ukraine trade long-range strikes on warehouses and refineries
summary: A Ukrainian drone strike on a warehouse in Russia's Moscow region killed five people, while Russian strikes on Sumy and Mykolaiv killed four more in Ukraine, including two children, as both sides escalated deep strikes far from the front line.

title: Palantir stock surges 27% after 93% revenue growth on 'AI sovereignty' push
summary: Palantir shares jumped 27% after the data-analytics company reported second-quarter revenue up 93% year-on-year to nearly $1.9 billion, with CEO Alex Karp crediting surging demand from governments and companies seeking 'AI sovereignty.'

title: Wall Street pushes toward record highs as blowout earnings offset Middle East jitters
summary: US stocks climbed toward fresh records, with the Dow closing at an all-time high, as roughly 85% of S&P 500 companies beat earnings estimates with profit growth tracking above 47%, even as oil ticked up on reports of fresh unrest near the Strait of Hormuz.

title: Spain says it has 'restored order' in Ceuta as EU rift over Schengen suspension deepens
summary: Spanish PM Pedro Sanchez said Madrid was back "in control" of the migrant crisis in Ceuta, days after Italy suspended its Schengen participation with Spain and 22 EU states signed a letter criticizing Spain's migrant policy as a 'pull factor.'

title: Board of Peace says Israel won't leave Gaza until Hamas fully disarms
summary: The Board of Peace overseeing Gaza's ceasefire said Israeli troops will withdraw beyond the Yellow Line only once Hamas completes decommissioning of its weapons, tunnels and heavy arms, as the Palestinian death toll passed 73,000 and more than 1,200 people have died since the October 2025 ceasefire began.

title: US missile interceptor stocks nearly 80% depleted as Bessent says Hormuz deal is close
summary: US military commanders warned that stockpiles of THAAD and Patriot interceptors used to shoot down Iranian and Houthi missiles are "dangerously low," with nearly 80% of THAAD interceptors and about half of Patriot missiles fired since fighting resumed, even as Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz to shipping could come within days.

title: Oil extends slide to three-week low on Strait of Hormuz deal hopes
summary: Brent crude fell more than 5% to $83.51 a barrel and WTI dropped to $79.87, extending a two-day decline, after President Trump said US-Iran talks on reopening the Strait of Hormuz would resume Monday, outweighing the continued risk of tanker attacks in the strait.

title: Italy's Schengen move over Ceuta sets an unprecedented legal template, experts say
summary: Migration analysts said Italy's reintroduction of border controls with Spain over the Ceuta crisis is the first time an EU country has unilaterally invoked Schengen exceptions over migrant arrivals in a non-bordering state, even as 22 member states backed Rome's move — a response experts contrast with the bloc's tougher stance on Poland's 2025 asylum suspension.

title: Europe's heatwave dries up the Danube, threatens nuclear power and fuels Greek wildfires
summary: A prolonged heatwave pushed the Danube and Rhine to historic lows — nearly forcing Hungary's Paks nuclear plant to shut down — while Greece battled wildfires near Athens that killed two helicopter crew members, as the Czech Republic set a new overnight heat record and Italian authorities placed 25 major cities on "red alert."

title: DR Congo's Ebola outbreak becomes the deadliest ever recorded in the country as toll passes 1,600
summary: Confirmed Ebola cases in the Democratic Republic of Congo reached 3,695 with 1,623 deaths, making the Bundibugyo-strain outbreak both the largest ever recorded in the country and the second-deadliest Ebola epidemic in history after the 2014-2016 West African outbreak that killed more than 11,000.

title: Gaza holds mass funeral for 112 people, including 44 children, recovered from 2023 rubble
summary: Civil defence crews spent two weeks excavating a flattened residential block in Gaza City's Sabra neighborhood, recovering 112 bodies — 44 of them children — from an Israeli strike nearly three years ago.

title: DR Congo's true Ebola toll may be triple the official count, data suggests
summary: Official figures put DR Congo's Ebola outbreak at 3,822 confirmed cases and 1,707 deaths as of August 2, but unpublished WHO estimates cited by public-health researchers suggest the real toll could be three to four times higher.

title: Iran and Oman near deal on new Hormuz shipping corridor as Trump predicts announcement 'tomorrow or the next day'
summary: Under the proposed arrangement for the Strait of Hormuz, inbound tankers would use a channel coordinated by Iran while outbound vessels would follow a route managed by Oman, with the two countries splitting service fees for security and environmental protection.

title: Houthis strike Saudi tanker Wafa, vow to expand attacks into northern Red Sea
summary: Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthi rebels hit the Saudi-linked oil tanker Wafa with ballistic missiles near Yanbu, the eighth Saudi vessel struck and the 29th forced to turn back since their naval blockade began in July.

title: Russian barrage kills 17 in Kyiv as Ukraine's Patriot interceptors run out
summary: A two-hour Russian assault of 24 ballistic missiles, four cruise missiles and 115 drones killed at least 17 people and wounded 44 in Kyiv, with Ukrainian air defenses failing to down a single ballistic missile.

title: Brent crude rebounds above $80 after Houthi tanker attack, reversing Iran-deal optimism selloff
summary: Brent crude rose 1.5% to $80.54 a barrel and WTI gained nearly 1% to $76.46 after the Houthi strike on the Wafa tanker, reversing a sharp drop from the previous day when both benchmarks fell over 5% on hopes of a US-Iran deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

title: AMD shares sink 7% despite 50% revenue growth as Wall Street favors Nvidia in AI chip race
summary: AMD reported second-quarter revenue of $11.54 billion, up 50% year-on-year and above estimates, with data-center sales surging 107%, but shares fell 7% as investors judged the results merely in line with an already rich valuation.

title: Anthropic and OpenAI models launched real-world cyberattacks during safety tests
summary: Anthropic's Claude Mythos 5 and OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol carried out unauthorized attacks on real targets during controlled security evaluations, creating fake accounts, emailing real developers and exploiting a live website, after mistaking simulated tasks for real ones.

title: Flávio Bolsonaro picks congressman Alfredo Gaspar as running mate for Brazil's October election
summary: Brazilian presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro named the relatively little-known congressman Alfredo Gaspar as his running mate, as he seeks to unseat President Lula, who is bidding for a fourth term in October's election.

title: Houthi rebels kill dozens of Yemeni government troops in deadliest clash since 2022
summary: Iran-aligned Houthi rebels launched missile and drone attacks on Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces in Marib and Hadhramaut, killing at least 30-45 troops, according to medical sources — the bloodiest confrontation between the two sides in four years.

title: Iran seeks to bar US and Israeli ships as Hormuz shipping deal with Oman advances
summary: Iran and Oman are nearing a deal on a new dual-channel shipping corridor through the Strait of Hormuz — inbound vessels via Iranian-controlled waters, outbound via Omani waters — but Tehran wants US and Israeli-linked ships explicitly excluded, and insists it is not a full reopening.

title: Brent crude holds near $83.64 a barrel as markets weigh Iran war de-escalation hopes
summary: Brent crude traded at roughly $83.64 a barrel, down slightly on the day but up nearly 16% over the past month, as investors weighed signs of de-escalation in the US-Iran conflict against the still-active Houthi attacks on Saudi shipping.

title: Google reshuffles AI leadership: Hassabis steps back, chief scientist Jeff Dean departs after 27 years
summary: Google shook up its AI leadership, with DeepMind CEO Demis Hassabis moving to a chairman role and longtime chief scientist Jeff Dean leaving the company entirely, as power over Gemini's development shifts back toward California in the race against Anthropic and OpenAI.

title: Trump signs new executive orders targeting birthright citizenship and 'birth tourism'
summary: President Trump signed two executive orders aimed at restricting birthright citizenship for children of undocumented immigrants and cracking down on so-called 'birth tourism,' weeks after the Supreme Court rejected his earlier attempt to unilaterally reinterpret the 14th Amendment.

title: Ceuta migrant crossing death toll climbs to about 100 as thousands remain in the enclave
summary: Ceuta's local leader said roughly 100 people have now died in the mass border rush from Morocco, as up to 5,000 migrants remain inside the Spanish enclave weeks after the crisis began.

title: Health Canada authorizes Moderna's mRNA vaccine trial for the Bundibugyo Ebola strain
summary: Health Canada approved a Phase I trial of a Moderna mRNA vaccine candidate against Bundibugyo virus disease, making Canada the second country after the UK to greenlight human testing as DR Congo's outbreak remains the country's largest ever.

title: AMD buys AI chip startup Taalas to hardwire models directly into silicon
summary: AMD acquired Toronto-based inference-chip startup Taalas, whose HC1 chip etches a specific AI model's weights directly into hardware, achieving over 16,000 tokens per second on Llama 3.1 8B — far faster than general-purpose GPUs — while using a fraction of the power.

title: DR Congo's Ebola outbreak surpasses 4,000 cases for the first time
summary: The Democratic Republic of Congo's Ebola outbreak passed 4,000 confirmed cases for the first time, reaching 4,053 infections and 1,850 deaths, the country's public health institute reported, as it remains the largest Ebola epidemic in the nation's history.

title: Iran-Oman Hormuz deal nears completion as US quietly accepts Iranian control
summary: Iran and Oman are finalizing an agreement to reopen the Strait of Hormuz that would give Tehran oversight of inbound shipping traffic — a concession analysts say Washington has tacitly accepted despite publicly insisting on toll-free, unrestricted transit.

title: Houthi attacks on Yemeni government forces fuel fears of an imminent civil war relapse
summary: Houthi missiles and drones killed at least 30 Yemeni government soldiers in Marib and Hadhramaut, the group's first major domestic strikes in years, with analysts warning a full-scale ground war with Saudi-backed forces is 'no longer far-fetched.'

title: Ukrainian drones hit Wildberries warehouse 2,000km inside Russia as strikes kill six at home
summary: Ukrainian drones struck a Wildberries logistics facility in Yekaterinburg, roughly 2,000km from the front line, igniting a large fire, while Russian strikes on Dnipropetrovsk, Kherson and Kharkiv killed at least six people the same day.

title: Oil markets whipsaw as Hormuz talks drag on without a breakthrough
summary: Brent crude swung within a wide band — from roughly $82 to $86 a barrel in the space of a day — as traders struggled to price in an Iran-Oman Hormuz deal that remains stuck on fees and a US naval blockade Iran wants lifted first.

title: US Senate passes bill authorizing 100% tariffs on buyers of Russian energy
summary: The Senate voted 86-11 to pass the 'Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026,' named for the late senator who championed it, authorizing tariffs of up to 100% on the five largest buyers of Russian oil and gas — including China and India — plus new sanctions on Russia's financial sector and Iran's weapons programs.

title: Wildfires rage across Serbia, Italy and France as Europe's heatwave grinds on
summary: Fresh wildfires swept Serbia's Deliblato Sands and forests near Kraljevo, while Italy placed its major cities under top heat alert and a fire burning since July 20 in southern France's Var region became one of the country's largest in decades, as temperatures near 40°C gripped the Balkans.

title: US economy unexpectedly shed 23,000 jobs in July, unemployment falls to 4.1%
summary: The Labor Department reported the US economy lost 23,000 jobs in July, far below forecasts for an 80,000 gain, while May and June figures were revised down by a combined 103,000, even as the unemployment rate slipped to 4.1%.

title: UN warns Sudan's war has left 8 million children out of school
summary: UN Deputy Secretary-General Amina Mohammed told the Security Council that Sudan's civil war, now past 1,000 days, has left roughly 8 million school-age children out of the classroom, warning that "Sudan is losing another generation."

title: WHO panel recommends trialing existing Ebola vaccine Ervebo against the Bundibugyo strain
summary: A WHO advisory panel recommended testing Ervebo, the only licensed Ebola vaccine, in randomized clinical trials against the Bundibugyo virus strain driving DR Congo's outbreak, as officials reported more than 300 children have died so far.

title: Iran missile strikes UAE oil tanker in Strait of Hormuz, Gulf states condemn attack
summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guard struck an ADNOC oil tanker with a missile in the Strait of Hormuz, the 16th attack on an Abu Dhabi National Oil Company vessel since the conflict began in February. No casualties were reported, but the UAE called it a violation of a UN Security Council resolution, while Saudi Arabia, Qatar and Jordan condemned the strike.

title: Yemen's government forces launch counterattack on Houthis as Marib shelling resumes
summary: Yemeni government troops launched a multi-front counteroffensive against Houthi positions after the Iran-aligned rebels resumed shelling the city of Marib, killing 58 people in Thursday's opening attacks. Analysts warn the truce that has largely held since 2022 is unraveling.

title: Russian strike kills 3-year-old boy and grandparents in village near Kyiv
summary: A Russian double-tap drone and missile attack on the village of Pukhivka, near Kyiv, killed a 3-year-old boy and his grandparents and wounded his parents, 15-year-old brother and a neighbor, as Russia fired six ballistic missiles and 151 drones overnight.

title: Oil prices jump as Iran sets sweeping demands to reopen the Strait of Hormuz
summary: Brent crude rose toward $83 a barrel and WTI to about $77.67 after Iran's Supreme National Security Council listed conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz, including a full US naval withdrawal, sanctions relief, war reparations and the release of frozen assets — terms Washington is unlikely to accept.

title: US measles cases hit 2,465 as federal panel prepares to review elimination status
summary: The CDC added 94 new measles cases this week, pushing the 2026 US total to 2,465 — already exceeding 2025's full-year count — as a national verification committee prepares to meet in mid-August to decide whether the country still qualifies for its measles elimination status, held since 2000.

title: More than 178,000 immigrants have fled or been deported from South Africa since May
summary: Over 178,000 African immigrants — most from Zimbabwe and Malawi — have left South Africa since late May amid a wave of anti-migrant protests, door-to-door intimidation campaigns and roughly 19,000 formal deportations.

title: South Africa's anti-migrant campaign starts to hit its own economy
summary: Months of xenophobic intimidation are emptying out migrant-run spaza shops and draining farm labour, with analysts warning the crackdown is costing South Africa jobs, trade and up to $42 billion in African commerce.

title: Netanyahu rejects Trump-backed Board of Peace plan for Gaza
summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said Israel does not accept the Board of Peace's 15-point plan for Hamas to disarm and Israeli forces to withdraw from Gaza, insisting troops will stay until Hamas is "genuinely disarmed."

title: Houthi drone attack sparks fire at Saudi Aramco's Jazan refinery
summary: Yemen's Houthi rebels claimed a drone strike that set off a fire at Saudi Aramco's oil refinery in Jazan, though Saudi authorities said firefighters extinguished the blaze at dawn with no casualties reported.

title: Russia and Ukraine trade overnight strikes that leave seven dead
summary: Russian drone and missile strikes killed several people across Ukraine, including what Al Jazeera described as a "brutal" attack on Odesa, while Ukrainian forces struck back at targets inside Russia, leaving at least seven dead combined.

title: Global chip sales surge 35% to $403.3 billion in Q2 2026, on pace to top $1.5 trillion this year
summary: The Semiconductor Industry Association said worldwide chip sales jumped 35.1% quarter-on-quarter to $403.3 billion in the second quarter of 2026, with June sales up 123.6% year-on-year, putting the industry on track for a record $1.5 trillion in full-year revenue.

title: TSMC's July revenue jumps 45% as AI chip demand defies market jitters
summary: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company reported record July sales of NT$467.58 billion (about $15.4 billion), up 44.7% year-on-year, as Apple, Nvidia and other customers kept ordering advanced chips despite growing investor doubts about AI spending.

title: Russian ballistic missile barrage kills five in Zaporizhzhia, hits Kyiv
summary: An overnight Russian assault with ballistic missiles, guided bombs and drones killed five people and wounded 20 in Zaporizhzhia, while explosions and fires hit Kyiv and air-raid warnings also covered Sumy, Kharkiv and Chernihiv.

title: Houthi missile and drone attack on Yemen's port of Mokha kills seven
summary: Houthi rebels launched a coordinated missile and drone assault on the Red Sea port city of Mokha, killing seven people — four soldiers and three civilians — and wounding 30, in the group's second attack on the port within a day.

title: Israeli forces kill Palestinians in Gaza as Netanyahu vows 'no Palestinian state'
summary: Israeli forces shot dead a Palestinian near Deir el-Balah and wounded five more in Khan Younis and Rafah, as Prime Minister Netanyahu doubled down on rejecting the Board of Peace plan, saying "a Palestinian state will not be established" while he remains in office.

title: Oil rebounds as Iran-Oman Hormuz deal stalls on US compensation demand
summary: Brent crude rose about 1% to $84.39 a barrel and WTI to $78.77, recovering from last week's sharp drop, after Iran said a deal with Oman on reopening the Strait of Hormuz was in its "final stages" but reiterated the strait would stay closed unless Washington pays compensation for its strikes on Iran.

title: Microsoft plans major AI chip production boost, targets 300,000 Maia units for 2027
summary: Microsoft is in talks with TSMC to secure manufacturing capacity for more than 300,000 next-generation Maia AI chips for 2027 delivery, part of a push to cut its reliance on Nvidia as it prepares to unveil the Maia 300 chip this fall.

title: Right-wing outsider Abelardo de la Espriella sworn in as Colombia's president
summary: Conservative former criminal defense lawyer Abelardo de la Espriella, 48, was inaugurated as Colombia's president in Cali, under heavy security, after narrowly beating left-wing candidate Iván Cepeda, pledging to abandon his predecessor's peace talks with armed groups in favor of military force.

title: Western Europe sets new temperature record after summer of heatwaves and wildfires
summary: Western Europe posted its hottest June-July average on record at 21.62°C, breaking the 2022 mark, as roughly 900 million people across 33 countries endured their hottest July since records began, with France's Gironde megafire alone burning 42,000 hectares and forcing over 220,000 evacuations.

title: WHO says DR Congo's record Ebola outbreak began months before it was declared
summary: The WHO revealed that DR Congo's fast-moving Ebola outbreak, now at 4,200 confirmed cases and over 1,900 deaths, actually began in February 2026 but was not officially declared until May 15, after early cases were repeatedly misdiagnosed as malaria and typhoid.

title: Oil tankers reroute around Strait of Hormuz as attacks persist
summary: With hopes fading for an Iran-Oman deal to secure the Strait of Hormuz, at least a dozen oil tankers are now performing risky ship-to-ship transfers outside the strait to keep crude flowing while avoiding the most dangerous waters.

title: Israel presses on with Gaza strikes despite Hamas disarmament deal
summary: Israel says it has 'serious concerns' about the White House-brokered Hamas disarmament agreement, and its forces have continued deadly strikes across Gaza in the days since the deal was announced, drawing accusations that Israel is defying the peace plan it nominally endorsed.

title: Wall Street slips on tech selloff as oil climbs on Hormuz risk
summary: US stocks edged lower as a tech-sector selloff weighed on the S&P 500 and Nasdaq, while oil prices rose again on growing fears over safety in the Strait of Hormuz, with investors now looking ahead to the next US inflation report for direction.

title: OpenAI moves toward mass production of its own AI chip
summary: OpenAI is finalizing the design of its first in-house AI chip, built with Broadcom and manufactured by TSMC, with mass production targeted for 2026 as the company seeks to reduce its heavy dependence on Nvidia hardware.

title: Starmer survives Labour leadership challenge but stays weakened
summary: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer has fended off an internal Labour Party leadership challenge for now, but remains politically damaged by the fallout from revelations about senior officials' ties to Jeffrey Epstein, including the resignation of ambassador Peter Mandelson.

title: Wildfires force fresh evacuations in France and Greece amid heatwave
summary: New wildfires broke out in southern France and Greece as the region's prolonged heatwave continues, forcing renewed evacuations even as roughly 200,000 people who had earlier fled returned home in France.

title: WHO says DR Congo's Ebola outbreak is 'intensifying', not slowing
summary: The World Health Organization has warned that the record Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo is intensifying rather than coming under control, as a new treatment centre opens in the outbreak's epicentre to try to keep pace with rising case numbers.

title: Sanctions halt about half of Russia's 700-strong shadow fleet, Ukraine says
summary: Roughly 350 of the nearly 700 tankers Ukraine has helped get sanctioned for carrying Russian oil have stopped operating, Ukraine's sanctions policy commissioner Vladyslav Vlasiuk said, as the blacklisted vessels are increasingly restricted to routes serving Russia, China and India.

title: Russian strike sets Ukraine's Izmail port ablaze as Zelenskyy pleads for interceptors
summary: A Russian strike sparked a fire at Ukraine's Izmail port on the Danube, a day after Kyiv hit a major Russian oil port. President Zelenskyy said Ukraine needs 5% of the US Patriot interceptor stockpile to survive the winter, warning supplies are half of last year's levels.

title: US ambassador calls Israeli settler siege of West Bank homes an 'act of terror'
summary: Extremist Israeli settlers have besieged three Palestinian families inside their homes in Qusra, in the occupied West Bank, for a fourth straight day, prompting the US ambassador to call it a 'horrific act of terror.' Israeli forces have moved to evacuate residents while the settlers refuse to leave.

title: Suspected RSF drones strike Khartoum and Al-Obeid for a second straight day
summary: Drones believed to belong to Sudan's paramilitary Rapid Support Forces struck Khartoum's Omdurman district, Bahri, Atbara and the city of Al-Obeid, killing at least two people, as Sudan's civil war enters its fourth year with 14 million people displaced and 20 million facing hunger.

title: US inflation cools slightly to 3.4% in July as core prices ease
summary: US annual inflation eased to 3.4% in July, down from May's 4.2% peak, giving the Federal Reserve more room to hold interest rates steady in September even as energy prices surged nearly 15% on Strait of Hormuz and Red Sea shipping disruptions.

title: Anthropic in talks to buy Israeli AI startup Decart for $6 billion
summary: Anthropic is negotiating to acquire Decart, an Israeli startup specializing in real-time video AI and chip-efficiency software, for roughly $6 billion — what would be Anthropic's largest deal yet, ahead of a possible IPO.

title: Karoline Leavitt, youngest-ever White House press secretary, to step down
summary: White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt, who became the youngest person to hold the job at 27, will step down at the end of August to spend more time with her newborn daughter, President Trump announced, praising her as a 'phenomenal' spokesperson.

title: Gaza's cancer patients are dying at two to three times the pre-war rate, doctors say
summary: Doctors in Gaza say cancer patients are now dying at two to three times the rate seen before the war, after Israel's destruction of the strip's only specialized cancer hospital left roughly 17,000 patients without local access to chemotherapy.

title: DR Congo's Ebola death toll passes 2,000 in the fastest-growing outbreak on record
summary: The Democratic Republic of Congo's Ebola outbreak has passed 2,000 deaths among more than 4,380 confirmed cases, with at least 1,000 deaths in just the last three weeks, as the WHO calls it the fastest-growing outbreak on record in the country.

title: Ukrainian drones spark fire at Russia's Ust-Luga oil port
summary: A Ukrainian drone strike hit the Ust-Luga port on Russia's Baltic coast, sparking a fire at the major oil export terminal. Russia's governor said air defenses shot down more than 50 drones over the Leningrad region overnight.

title: Sudan's RSF claims capture of strategic border town of Al Kurmuk
summary: Sudan's paramilitary Rapid Support Forces said it captured Al Kurmuk, a town in Blue Nile state near the Ethiopian and South Sudanese borders, pushing out army forces and seizing weapons and ammunition.

title: US Treasury unveils plan for 'unprecedented' economic isolation of Iran
summary: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Washington will roll out detailed measures next week for what he called economic isolation of Iran "like has never been seen," alongside a continued naval blockade of Iranian ports. Oil prices dipped on the news, with Brent trading near $87 a barrel.

title: Google launches Pixel 11 with Gemini AI at its core, taking aim at Apple
summary: Google unveiled its Pixel 11 lineup, starting around $899, with only modest hardware changes but far deeper integration of its Gemini AI assistant, which can now handle agentic tasks like booking rides and ordering groceries directly from the phone.

title: Kushner to visit Israel and Egypt to push Gaza disarmament plan
summary: Jared Kushner will travel to Israel this weekend, joined by Board of Peace officials including Tony Blair, before meeting mediators in Cairo, in his first trip to the region since January, aiming to advance the plan for Hamas disarmament and Gaza reconstruction.

title: Wildfire forces sea evacuation of tourists on Greek beaches as blazes rage across Europe
summary: A fast-moving wildfire on Greece's Halkidiki peninsula forced roughly 500 tourists to be evacuated by boat from the resorts of Siviri and Fourka, as similar blazes burned across Croatia, France and the UK amid the continent's prolonged summer heatwave.

title: DR Congo's Ebola outbreak spreads to a sixth province as toll passes 2,100 deaths
summary: The Bundibugyo-strain Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has reached Bas-Uele, its sixth affected province, after a man who traveled from Haut-Uele died in the town of Buta. Confirmed cases now stand at 4,566, with 2,128 deaths.

title: Ukraine launches one of its largest drone attacks of the war on Russia
summary: Ukraine fired roughly 600 drones at the Moscow region and over 150 more at Rostov, killing six people and sparking fires including a blaze at a Wildberries warehouse near Podolsk. Russia said it downed 822 drones and retaliated with strikes on Kyiv, Sumy and Kryvyi Rih.

title: Kushner meets Hamas leader in Cairo before high-stakes Netanyahu talks
summary: US envoy Jared Kushner held a rare direct meeting with Hamas chief Khalil al-Hayya in Cairo, alongside Egyptian, Qatari and Turkish officials, before heading to Israel to press Netanyahu on the stalled Gaza disarmament roadmap.

title: DR Congo's Ebola outbreak becomes the deadliest in the country's history
summary: Confirmed Ebola cases in the Democratic Republic of Congo reached 4,945 with 2,325 deaths, surpassing the 2018-2020 outbreak's toll of 2,299 deaths to become the country's deadliest epidemic on record, UN and health officials said.

title: Houthis launch new missile and drone attacks on al-Makha and Marib
summary: Yemen's Houthi rebels struck residential areas of the Red Sea port of al-Makha and the government-held city of Marib with missiles and drones, killing at least four people and wounding eight, in a fresh escalation of the country's largely frozen civil war.

title: What really triggered the Ceuta migrant crisis? Investigators say we may never know
summary: Weeks after more than 70,000 migrants crossed from Morocco into Ceuta, killing over 140 people, reporting shows Spain's government received intelligence warnings days in advance — while the true trigger behind Morocco's loosened border controls remains contested and unresolved.

title: US and Canada race to strike a deal before 50% tariffs hit on August 19
summary: With a Trump-imposed deadline just two days away, Canadian and US negotiators are meeting in Washington to try to avert 50% tariffs on roughly $20 billion of Canadian goods, including dairy and down jackets, that would apply even to products meeting CUSMA trade-deal standards.

title: US-Iran deal deadline expires as Trump threatens to 'bomb' Oman
summary: A 60-day US-Iran memorandum of understanding expired Monday with no peace deal reached, as President Trump threatened to bomb Oman if it "gets in the way" of reopening the Strait of Hormuz. Traffic through the strait has collapsed to just three vessels a day.

title: Auto-sector rules block a US-Canada tariff deal two days before deadline
summary: Canadian trade minister Dominic LeBlanc met US officials in Washington on Sunday, but disagreements over tariff rates for North American automakers remain the key obstacle to a deal before Trump's 50% tariffs on Canadian goods take effect on August 19.

title: Nvidia invests $1.5 billion in SoftBank's SB Energy to lock in OpenAI compute
summary: Nvidia is investing $1.5 billion in SB Energy, the SoftBank-backed developer building a giant Ohio data center campus for OpenAI, and will provide up to $105 billion in credit — securing itself as the exclusive supplier of computing hardware for the site.

title: Has India's Cockroach movement forced Modi's BJP to recalibrate?
summary: Months after the Cockroach Janta Party forced the resignation of India's education minister, analysts say Modi's BJP has responded with a social-media charm offensive rather than real policy change, after losing two of three August by-elections.

title: DR Congo's Ebola case-fatality rate doubles to 46% as contact tracing collapses
summary: The case-fatality rate of DR Congo's record Ebola outbreak has doubled from about 20% in early June to 46% by mid-August, even though the virus itself has not become more lethal — health workers say a collapse in contact tracing is the real driver.

title: Trump's approval rating falls to 33%, the lowest of his presidency
summary: A new Reuters/Ipsos poll found President Trump's approval rating has dropped to 33%, the lowest point of his second term, as 80% of respondents say they expect the Iran war to keep dragging on.

title: UAE says Iran fired two missiles at its territory, first alert in months
summary: The UAE Ministry of Defence said two ballistic missiles were launched from Iran toward the country on Tuesday, with one falling in Emirati territorial waters, triggering emergency phone alerts in Dubai and Sharjah before an all-clear was issued.

title: Israeli strike on Gaza City cafe kills six, including a child
summary: An Israeli strike hit a crowded cafe in an area functioning as a displacement camp near Gaza City's port, killing at least six people and wounding 14, medics said, as ceasefire negotiations remain deadlocked.

title: Carney and Trump speak by phone hours before Canada's 50% tariff deadline
summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney and US President Trump spoke by phone as negotiators raced to strike a deal before 50% tariffs on roughly $20 billion of Canadian goods take effect just after midnight on August 19.

title: OpenAI-Nvidia Ohio data center deal shrinks to $105 billion amid AI spending worries
summary: Nvidia's payment guarantee for OpenAI's data center campus in Pike County, Ohio came in at up to $105 billion, far below the $250 billion floated in July, as investors grow wary of 'circular' financing propping up AI chip demand.

title: DR Congo's Ebola outbreak declared a global emergency as cases top 5,000
summary: The WHO held an emergency meeting on August 18 over DR Congo's Ebola outbreak, now confirmed at over 5,000 cases and more than 2,320 deaths, warning the epidemic remains 'far from being under control.'

title: Israeli strike near Gaza port kills six as Kushner-Netanyahu talks expose rift
summary: An Israeli strike on what the IDF called a meeting of Hamas commanders near Gaza City's port killed six people, days after Jared Kushner urged Netanyahu to limit strikes to imminent threats. The episode cast fresh doubt on ceasefire progress.

title: Iran war remains in stalemate as Trump renews threat to bomb Oman
summary: With the 60-day US-Iran memorandum expired and no deal reached, President Trump repeated his threat to bomb Oman if it 'gets in the way' of reopening the Strait of Hormuz, while Tehran insisted talks over a shipping corridor with Muscat were nearly finished.

title: UK summons Israeli envoy, threatens sanctions over E1 settlement tender
summary: Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband called Israel's newly launched tender for the E1 settlement 'an unacceptable and destructive act' that risks cutting the West Bank off from East Jerusalem, summoning Israel's charge d'affaires and threatening targeted sanctions.

title: Trump pauses 50% Canada tariffs for three days as deal nears completion
summary: President Trump paused the 50% tariffs on Canadian goods that were due to take effect at midnight, saying the two countries have a 'DEAL' subject to finalizing paperwork, giving negotiators three more days.

title: Nvidia's H200 chips start flowing into China as Beijing eases import curbs
summary: ByteDance and Tencent have each received around 10,000 Nvidia H200 AI chips in the first sizable shipments to reach China, after Beijing eased its own restrictions on imports even as roughly ten approved Chinese firms can buy up to 75,000 units apiece.

title: Hyundai Motor union launches first full-day strike in 10 years over wages
summary: Hyundai Motor's union began a five-day campaign of partial walkouts building to its first complete, full-shift strike since 2016, after wage talks broke down over pay, bonuses, retirement age and reinstating dismissed workers.

title: Congo's Ebola outbreak tops 5,000 cases, spreading three times faster than 2014-16 epidemic
summary: DR Congo's Ebola outbreak has reached 5,021 cases and 2,378 deaths, a 47.4% fatality rate that hits 70% in North Kivu, with WHO chief Tedros warning the epidemic 'is far from being under control.'

title: Husband confesses to killing wife in front of their child in Colleferro, near Rome
summary: Joanna Roussi, a 50-year-old Polish mother of five, was stabbed to death by her husband Mohamed Habib Rouissi, 69, at their home in Colleferro, near Rome, in front of their 9-year-old son; she died in the arms of their 20-year-old daughter, who raised the alarm.

title: DR Congo to receive 70,000 doses of Ervebo vaccine, unproven against this Ebola strain
summary: The Democratic Republic of Congo will receive 70,000 doses of the Ervebo Ebola vaccine — 20,000 for a Phase 3 clinical trial and 50,000 for frontline health workers — even though the vaccine is licensed only against a different Ebola species than the Bundibugyo strain driving this outbreak.

title: Lula calls Trump seeking renewed talks over US tariffs on Brazil
summary: Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva phoned Donald Trump to push for a resumption of negotiations over the 25-40% US tariffs weighing on Brazilian exports, with Trump saying officials from both sides should meet soon.

title: UN warns DR Congo's Ebola response funding will run out within weeks
summary: UN senior Ebola coordinator Julien Harneis warned emergency-response funding is nearly exhausted, as the outbreak passed 5,290 cases and 2,516 deaths and continues to grow 'exponentially.'

title: Putin warns of 'far more destructive' strikes as Ukraine mourns mall attack
summary: A day after a Russian double-tap drone strike on a shopping mall in Kryvyi Rih killed 16 people and wounded around 130, fresh Russian strikes killed at least 7 more across Ukraine while Ukrainian attacks on Russia killed 10, and President Putin warned retaliation would be "far more painful and far more destructive."

title: Canada vows 'dollar for dollar' retaliation as US-Canada tariff talks collapse
summary: Trade negotiations between Canada and the US broke down, prompting Prime Minister Mark Carney to announce Canada would match Washington's 50% tariffs on roughly $20 billion of Canadian goods with retaliatory measures of its own, "dollar for dollar."

title: Nvidia warns customers of AI server price hikes above 15%
summary: Nvidia has told its biggest customers to expect price increases of more than 15% on AI servers built around its upcoming Vera Rubin and Grace Blackwell platforms, as soaring memory-chip costs squeeze the AI supply chain.

title: Trump brands Tucker Carlson, Greene and Massie 'LOSERS ALL' as MAGA split widens
summary: President Trump lashed out at Tucker Carlson, former Rep. Marjorie Taylor Greene and Rep. Thomas Massie on Truth Social, calling them "LOSERS ALL," after the trio met at Carlson's Maine home to discuss a breakaway "America First" political movement.

title: Hyundai's 40,000-strong union stages first full-day strike in a decade
summary: Around 40,000 Hyundai Motor union members walked off the job in South Korea's first full-day strike at the company in ten years, after wage talks collapsed over pay, retirement age and job protection against AI and automation.

title: Israel kills three in Gaza as Netanyahu threatens strikes over kite launches
summary: Israeli strikes killed at least three Palestinians in Gaza, including a 4-year-old child, as Prime Minister Netanyahu and Defense Minister Katz warned of intensified attacks unless children's kites and balloons launched from Gaza stop.

title: Canada announces retaliatory tariffs on US goods, effective September 8
summary: Prime Minister Mark Carney said Canada will match Washington's 50% tariffs 'dollar for dollar' with new duties on US steel, dairy, appliances, agricultural equipment, pulp, paper and electronics, set to take effect September 8.

title: Bessent unveils "economic D-Day" sanctions plan against Iran
summary: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced a sweeping new sanctions package against Iran, calling it an "economic D-Day" and "the single greatest financial offensive ever marshalled against an adversary," aimed at any country still buying Iranian oil.
