title: Israeli strikes kill four in Gaza, including two children, a week after US urged restraint
summary: Israeli strikes and tank fire hit the Bureij and Shati refugee camps, Gaza City, Deir al-Balah and Khan Younis, killing at least four Palestinians, including two children aged 4 and 10.

title: Russia strikes Ukraine on its 35th Independence Day as European leaders visit Kyiv
summary: Russia fired 72 drones and a ballistic missile at Ukraine overnight on Independence Day, killing three people, as UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham and other European leaders arrived in Kyiv to show solidarity.

title: Supreme Court lets Trump's mail-in ballot restrictions move forward ahead of midterms
summary: The Supreme Court handed the Trump administration a preliminary win, allowing parts of an executive order restricting mail-in balloting to proceed while litigation continues, months before the midterm elections.

title: Nasdaq slips as Micron falls 6% heading into Nvidia's earnings week
summary: US tech stocks retreated, with Micron shares dropping about 6-7%, as investors braced for Nvidia's closely watched quarterly results on August 26 and the Federal Reserve's Jackson Hole gathering.

title: DR Congo's record Ebola outbreak passes 100 days, with 5,515 cases and 2,642 deaths
summary: One hundred days after being declared, DR Congo's Bundibugyo-strain Ebola outbreak has reached 5,515 confirmed cases and 2,642 deaths, a roughly 48% fatality rate, WHO chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said the epidemic can still be brought under control.

title: Ottawa police identify 27-year-old woman killed in weekend femicide
summary: Kesi Fevrier, 27, was found dead at a home in Ottawa's Lowertown neighbourhood over the weekend; police are investigating her death as a femicide, the city's third of 2026 and ninth homicide overall.

title: Hyundai union reaches tentative wage deal, ending its first full strike in a decade
summary: Hyundai Motor's South Korean union reached a tentative agreement with management, including a monthly base pay rise, a bonus worth 400% of base salary, and 500 new technical hires through 2028, ending the standoff that produced the company's first full-day strike since 2016.

title: Israeli strike destroys Gaza aid warehouse storing supplies for malnourished children
summary: An Israeli strike destroyed a humanitarian warehouse in Gaza storing nutrition supplies for children, pregnant women and nursing mothers, as separate strikes across the strip killed seven Palestinians.

title: Trump sends Saudi nuclear deal to Congress, ties it to Israel recognition
summary: The Trump administration submitted a 30-year civil nuclear cooperation agreement with Saudi Arabia to Congress, but says the deal will only move forward if Riyadh joins the Abraham Accords and recognizes Israel.

title: Indian police clash with job-seeking protesters in Patna, a month after Gen Z marches
summary: Police used water cannon and batons against thousands of protesters marching on the Bihar chief minister's residence over stalled civil-service exam recruitment, a month after youth-led Gen Z demonstrations shook Delhi.

title: Ukrainian drones destroy Wildberries warehouse in Russia's Tambov region, kill three
summary: A large Ukrainian drone attack set ablaze a Wildberries e-commerce warehouse in Kotovsk, Tambov region, destroying roughly 100,000 square metres, while separate strikes killed three people in Lipetsk and Belgorod.

title: Nvidia posts record $96 billion quarter, Huang forecasts 70% revenue growth for fiscal 2028
summary: Nvidia reported record second-quarter revenue of roughly $96 billion, more than double a year earlier, and gave a rare year-ahead forecast of 70% revenue growth for fiscal 2028, seeking to quiet fears of an AI spending bubble.

title: Flash floods from Himalayan glacial collapse kill over 160 in Nepal, hundreds missing on Tibet border
summary: A glacial collapse triggered flash floods and mudslides along the Nepal-Tibet border, killing at least 162 people in Nepal and leaving 558 missing in Tibet, including 260 foreign nationals, after water levels rose nine metres in just 30 minutes.

title: Italian cabinet extends fuel-price discount and moves to unblock Ex Ilva waste management
summary: Italy's Council of Ministers, chaired by PM Giorgia Meloni, held a brief post-summer session extending the 17-cent-per-litre discount on diesel until September 5 and approving a decree to unblock waste-management operations at the former Ilva steelworks.

title: Nepal flood death toll reaches 160 as rescuers recover 157 bodies, hundreds still missing
summary: A day after the glacial flash flood on the Nepal-Tibet border, rescuers have recovered 157 bodies and the confirmed death toll has reached 160, with hundreds of people — including 34 Australians and 33 Americans — still unaccounted for.

title: Nvidia shares slip despite record earnings as Wall Street questions AI valuations
summary: Nvidia stock fell roughly 1% in after-hours trading even after revenue surged 106% year-on-year to $96.2 billion and the company projected $108 billion in third-quarter sales, as investors weighed renewed concerns about AI-sector valuations.

title: Israel reportedly weighs expelling British officials from Gaza coordination center
summary: Israel is considering expelling British officials — and possibly other European representatives — from the International Gaza Support Center, the multinational hub overseeing the US-brokered ceasefire, according to a Financial Times report.

title: Russia launches 'massive' overnight strike on 9 Ukrainian cities
summary: Russia says it carried out a large-scale missile and drone attack on nine Ukrainian cities overnight, in one of the broadest single strikes of the war in recent months.

title: OpenAI, Anthropic and 100+ companies call for defenses against 'rogue AI'
summary: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and more than 100 other companies signed a joint call urging governments and industry to build stronger defenses against AI systems being misused for cyberattacks.

title: Zelenskyy orders Ukraine's army to launch 1,000 drones a day at Russia
summary: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy held a command meeting and ordered Ukraine's military to scale up long-range drone production so it can launch 1,000 drones a day against targets inside Russia.

title: Marvell shares tumble 6% despite beat-and-raise quarter, as AI chip investors grow wary
summary: Marvell Technology stock dropped about 6% even after the chipmaker beat second-quarter earnings estimates and raised its revenue outlook, as investors questioned how quickly its custom-chip deal with Google will pay off.

title: The EU's AI Act enforcement starts to bite for OpenAI, Google and Anthropic
summary: Weeks after new EU AI Act transparency and enforcement rules took effect, companies including OpenAI, Google and Anthropic are now facing real compliance deadlines and potential fines, as Brussels starts actively policing how general-purpose AI models are labeled and disclosed.

title: Italy's League party readies bill to block new mosques and Islamic centers
summary: Deputy PM Matteo Salvini's League party said it has a bill ready to stop new Islamic religious sites from opening in Italy, reigniting a national debate after a local dispute over a planned mosque near Venice.

title: Thousands march in Washington to defend voting and civil rights
summary: Thousands of demonstrators marched in Washington, D.C., joined by lawmakers including Hakeem Jeffries and Bernie Sanders, warning that voting rights and other civil-rights protections are being rolled back.

title: Congo's record Ebola outbreak may be three times larger than reported, Africa CDC warns
summary: Africa CDC officials said the true scale of the Democratic Republic of Congo's already-record Ebola outbreak could be up to three times higher than the official case count, due to gaps in surveillance and contact tracing in the hardest-hit regions.

title: Italian man arrested after German partner found stabbed to death on Spanish beach
summary: An Italian man has been arrested in Huelva, Andalusia, accused of fatally stabbing his 47-year-old German partner during what was meant to be a camper-van trip along Spain's southern coast.

title: One killed, one seriously wounded in shooting ambush in Calabria
summary: A 34-year-old man was shot dead and another man was left seriously wounded in an ambush near a bar in Lauropoli, in the Cassano allo Ionio area of Calabria's Cosenza province.

title: Italian man arrested after German woman is stabbed to death in southern Spain
summary: Spain's Guardia Civil arrested a 60-year-old Italian man on suspicion of stabbing his 47-year-old German partner to death on a street in Isla Cristina, in Huelva province, while the couple were on a camper-van holiday in Andalusia.

title: Russian strike near Kyiv kills 37 in one of the war's deadliest attacks this year
summary: A Russian strike hit a warehouse holding ammunition on the outskirts of Kyiv, triggering a chain of explosions that killed at least 37 people and wounded dozens more, in one of the deadliest single attacks of the year.

title: Ukraine says Russia is planning a ground offensive toward Kyiv and Chernihiv
summary: Ukraine's deputy chief of staff, Pavlo Palisa, said intelligence indicates the Kremlin has ordered planning for a possible ground offensive aimed at Kyiv and Chernihiv, though he said there is no evidence yet of an offensive force actually massing.

title: Israeli strikes and fire kill three Palestinians in Gaza despite ceasefire framework
summary: Israeli military strikes and tank fire killed three Palestinians in Gaza on Saturday, including a motorbike strike in Gaza City and a farmer killed by tank fire near Deir al-Balah, as violence continues despite the ceasefire framework in place since October.

title: Wall Street ends the week lower as Fed Chair Warsh raises rate-hike odds at Jackson Hole
summary: U.S. stocks fell and traders raised the odds of a Federal Reserve rate hike after new Fed Chair Kevin Warsh used his keynote speech at the Jackson Hole symposium to warn that inflation remains too stubborn to justify near-term rate cuts.

title: Europe's AI debate turns to who is really in control, as Signal's Whittaker sounds the alarm
summary: At the TechBBQ conference in Copenhagen, European founders and investors debated how dependent Europe has become on U.S. and Chinese AI infrastructure, with Signal president Meredith Whittaker warning that folding AI agents into operating systems is creating a sweeping new "data collection apparatus."

title: Meloni attacks PD's Bonaccini over remarks linking right-wing votes to lower education
summary: Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni escalated a political row over comments by Democratic Party figure Stefano Bonaccini suggesting that right-wing voters in Italy, Europe and the U.S. tend to be less educated and economically struggling, calling the remarks disrespectful toward center-right voters.

title: Tunisia's Yezzi movement calls for more protests as heat wave worsens shortages
summary: Tunisia's grassroots Yezzi movement called for renewed street protests after a punishing heat wave caused deaths and triggered power and water cuts, compounding shortages of medicine and basic goods that have fueled two months of demonstrations against President Kais Saied.

title: DRC's record Ebola outbreak passes 5,700 cases and nearly 2,800 deaths
summary: The Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo, already the country's deadliest on record, has grown to 5,794 confirmed cases and 2,786 deaths, with the virus now present in 60 health zones across six provinces.

title: Cremona counts the damage after a tornado and hailstorm hit the city in ten minutes
summary: The city of Cremona is assessing widespread damage after a tornado accompanied by intense hail tore through the city center in about ten minutes, injuring 43 people and damaging ten churches, including the cathedral, which lost part of its spire.

title: Two young men from Genoa killed in highway tunnel crash in Piedmont
summary: Two men aged 23 and 22 from Genoa died after their rental car lost control inside the Giaglione tunnel on the A32 highway between Bardonecchia and Oulx, in Piedmont near the French border.

title: US strikes Iran's Larak Island in first attack in weeks, Iran hits back at Jordan bases
summary: The United States struck Iranian rocket launchers on Larak Island in the Strait of Hormuz on Sunday, its first military action against Iran in about a month, saying it acted to stop the IRGC from laying sea mines in the strait. Iran retaliated with missiles and drones against two US bases in Jordan, King Hussein and Al Azraq; Jordan said it intercepted eight missiles and no injuries were reported there.

title: Masked Israeli settlers storm West Bank village of Qusra, seize home with owner inside
summary: Dozens of masked Israeli settlers stormed the Palestinian village of Qusra in the occupied West Bank on August 29-30, attacking residents and foreign journalists, including an NBC crew, and seizing a Palestinian family's home with the owner still inside. Prime Minister Netanyahu publicly condemned the "rioters" after weeks of escalating settler violence in the area.

title: Israeli strike near Gaza bakery kills 3-year-old boy and one other, medics say
summary: An Israeli strike hit near a bakery in Deir al-Balah, central Gaza, on Sunday, killing Hussam Nusair and three-year-old Tayyem Hamdan and wounding several others, Gaza medics said. The Israeli military said it had "struck a Hamas militant" but gave no further details.

title: Two young men killed in three-motorcycle crash in Piedmont
summary: A collision involving three motorcycles on the SS25 state road in Giaglione, in the province of Turin, killed two young riders on Sunday: Luca Bramard, 21, from Mazzè, and Ivan Perron, 18, from Bussoleno. A third rider was injured and taken to hospital.

title: Woman stabbed to death in her home in San Giovanni al Natisone, husband arrested
summary: Chen Fengjiao, 54, was stabbed to death in her home in San Giovanni al Natisone, in the province of Udine, between August 29 and 30. Neighbours alerted police after hearing screams; her husband was detained on the spot and later arrested on charges of voluntary homicide.

title: Oil jumps as US strike on Iran's Larak Island reignites Strait of Hormuz fears
summary: Brent crude rose more than 2% back above $90 a barrel and WTI gained a similar margin after the US strike on Iran's Larak Island and Iran's retaliatory missile attack on US bases in Jordan, as traders priced in renewed risk to Gulf oil shipping. Traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, which normally carries about a fifth of global oil supply, has stayed low, with only a handful of tankers transiting daily.
